etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English aplien, applien, from Old French applier, (French appliquer), from Latin applicō (“join, fix, or attach to”); from ad + plicō (“fold, twist together”). See applicant, ply.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To lay or place; to put (one thing to another)

quote.citation: 1697, John Dryden, Translation of Virgil's Aeneid:
quote.text: He said, and to the sword his throat applied.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To put to use; to use or employ for a particular purpose, or in a particular case
(transitive) To make use of, declare, or pronounce, as suitable, fitting, or relative

quote.citation: 1667, John Milton, “Book X”, in Paradise Lost. […], London:  […]  [Samuel Simmons], and are to be sold by Peter Parker […]; [a]nd by Robert Boulter […]; [a]nd Matthias Walker, […], →OCLC; republished as Paradise Lost in Ten Books: […], London: Basil Montagu Pickering […], 1873, →OCLC:
quote.text: Yet God at last To Satan, first in sin, his doom applied.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To put closely; to join; to engage and employ diligently, or with attention

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Proverbs 23:12:
quote.text: Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To address; to refer; generally used reflexively.

quote.citation: 1725, Homer, “Book X”, in [Alexander Pope], transl., The Odyssey of Homer. […], volume III, London:  […]  Bernard Lintot, →OCLC:
quote.text: sacred vows  […]  applied to grisly Pluto

quote.citation: 1854 August 9, Henry D[avid] Thoreau, “Economy”, in Walden; or, Life in the Woods, Boston, Mass.: Ticknor and Fields, →OCLC:
quote.text: On applying to the assessors, I am surprised to learn that they cannot at once name a dozen in the town who own their farms free and clear.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To submit oneself as a candidate (with the adposition "to" designating the recipient of the submission, and the adposition "for" designating the position).

quote.citation: 1974 August 7, Ronald A. Frank, “SP Seeks Approval for Coast-to-Coast Digital Net”, in Computerworld, page 15:
quote.text: Southern Pacific Communications Co. (SP) has applied to the FCC for approval of the first coast-to-coast digital data transmission service.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To pertain or be relevant to a specified individual or group.
(obsolete) To busy; to keep at work; to ply.

quote.citation: a. 1587, Philippe Sidnei [i.e., Philip Sidney], “(please specify the folio)”, in [Fulke Greville; Matthew Gwinne; John Florio], editors, The Countesse of Pembrokes Arcadia [The New Arcadia], London:  […]  [John Windet] for William Ponsonbie, published 1590, →OCLC:
quote.text: She was no less skillful in applying his humours.

quote.citation: [1611?], Homer, “(please specify |book=I to XXIV)”, in Geo[rge] Chapman, transl., The Iliads of Homer Prince of Poets. […], London:  […]  Nathaniell Butter, →OCLC; republished as The Iliads of Homer, Prince of Poets, […], new edition, volume (please specify the book number), London: Charles Knight and Co., […], 1843, →OCLC:
quote.text: His armour was so clear,  And he applied each place so fast, that like a lightning thrown  Out of the shield of Jupiter, in every eye he shone.The spelling has been modernized.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From apple +‎ -y.
